title: He wasn’t told to admire faith.
paragraphs: He wasn’t told to admire faith.
He was told to fight for it.
“Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called…” — 1 Timothy 6:12

That means faith is not passive.
It bleeds.
It wrestles.
It stands when everything in you wants to quit.

Because some battles are not with swords.
They are with temptation.
Fear.
Secret compromise.
The voices that whisper, “Just give up. Just blend in. Just bow once.”

Paul did not say fight for popularity.
Fight for comfort.
Fight for applause.
He said fight the good fight of faith.

The good fight is the battle to keep trusting Jesus when money seduces, when lust stalks, when suffering confuses, and when your own heart feels tired. It is the war of holding on to Christ when the world offers cheaper saviors.
And you do not fight alone.

Jesus already won the decisive victory at the cross. He crushed sin’s claim, broke death’s sting, and rose again so weary sinners could stand in grace, not in their own strength. We fight from His victory, not for it.

So today, brother. Sister.
Do not surrender your soul for a temporary escape.

Pray again.
Repent again.
Stand again.
Believe again.

This is not the hour to drift.
This is the hour to take hold of eternal life and refuse to let hell, shame, or desire drag you back.

Fight.
Not with pride.
Not with panic.
But with faith in the Son of God.

And when your hands shake, remember:
the same Christ who calls you to fight is the Christ who keeps you.
